item.title: backlog add --ready silently skips readiness gate warnings that backlog edit --ready runs
item.intent: When creating an item with --ready, readiness gate warnings must be shown exactly as they are when using 'backlog edit <ID> --ready', so users get immediate feedback instead of a silent gotcha.
item.description: cmd_backlog_edit runs check_readiness_gates after setting readyForSprint=true via --ready, printing warnings if gates fail (while still allowing the operation). cmd_backlog_add has no equivalent check. A user who adds an item with --ready and no steps, no AC, or no intent sees 'Created BUG-XXX' with no indication that the item will fail 'backlog check'. This is inconsistent with 'backlog edit' and BUG-100 behavior — once auto warns on skipped items, users need to know at add-time too.
steps: After log_success 'Created $new_id' in cmd_backlog_add, check if ready==true
If ready is true, call check_readiness_gates "$new_id" and capture warnings
If gates fail, print the same warning format as cmd_backlog_edit: 'log_warning "Readiness warnings for $new_id:"; printf '%b\n' "$gates_warnings"'
Do not block item creation — warnings are advisory, matching edit behavior
acceptanceCriteria: Running 'backlog add --title X --ready' with no steps or AC prints readiness warnings after the Created success message
Running 'backlog add --title X --ready' with valid steps, AC, and intent prints no readiness warnings
Item is still created in both cases — warnings do not block creation
shellcheck passes with zero new warnings
